full_judgment: The suit property appertaining to Plot No. 4166 of SA Khatian No.1359 of Mouza-Wari, PS Sutrapur, Dhaka, measuring an area of 0.3080 acre with appurtenances originally belonged to Sreemoti Labanga Lata Chowdhury, wife of late Ramdulal Ganguly. On 19-2-1984, the suit property was requisitioned by the Government in Requisition Case Nos.192/48 and 3/4 share of the suit property was allotted to the husband of plaintiff No. 1, late Gowher Jamil and the remaining 1/4 share of the suit property to the father of plaintiff No. 2, late Lokman Hakim, while they were in service under the Government. While residing over the suit property Gowher Jamil, the husband of plaintiff No. 1 erected a semi pucca corrugated iron shed and started an institution in the name and style, Jago Art Centre. Subsequently, the husband of plaintiff No. 1 as a Director of Jago Art Center got allotment of 3/4 share of the suit property from defendant No. 3 in the name of Jago Art Center. Gowher Jamil started the Jago Art Center to impart dancing lessons in dance and to promote the culture of music and dance in the country. On 22-9-1980, Gowher Jamil, the Director of the Jago Art Center, died in a road accident and after his death, plaintiff No. 1 became the Director. On the death of Lokman Hakim, plaintiff No. 2 got allotment of the suitproperty who was also an employee. of the, Government. While in possession of the suit property, they got a notice from defendant No. 2, Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) (LA), Dhaka on 30-7-1985 and came to know that the suit property had been de-requisitioned in favour of its owner Harlal Ganguly on 22-2-1948 and the plaintiffs were directed to hand over possession of the suit property. After getting this notice, they became astonished as to how the suit property was de-requisitioned in favour of Harlal Ganguly, who died long before. After that, defendant No. 2, ADC (LA), Dhaka gave reminder to them to hand over possession of the suit property by 31-5-1986 failing which they would be evicted therefrom. But they did not hand over possession of the suit property in favour of defendant No.2, who again served a notice on 7-9-1986 to hand over possession of the suit property by 16-10-1986. Finding no other alternative, they filed Title Suit No. 201 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka on 28-6-1986, challenging the order of de-requisition dated 22-2-1986 and also the notice dated 7-9-1986. The suit was decreed ex parte on 18-4-1987 as the defendants did not file any written statement. Against the ex parte decree dated 18-4-1987, defendant Nos. 2-4 preferred Title Appeal No. 133 of 1987 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka who allowed the appeal setting aside the ex parte decree passed by the trial Court and also dismissed the suit on the ground of maintainability under section 14A of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. Harlal Ganguly during those long years did not come to the suit property and he also did not receive the rent of the suit property Defendant No. 1 has created a forged and collusive document in respect of the suit property on 1-6-1983 in the name of Harlal Ganguly and on the basis of this collusive document, he has been trying to mutate his name. Defendant No. 1 in collusion with defendant No. 2 managed to get the order of de-requisition of the suit property in favour of Harlal Ganguly on 22-2-1984. The order of de-requisition dated 22-2-1984 is collusive and illegal. Defendant Nos. 2-4 in collusion with defendant No. 1 have been trying to evict the plaintiffs from the suit property. The deed of sale dated 1-6-1983 in favour of defendant No. 1 by. Harlal Ganguly is collusive and forged and, as such, on the basis of this deed, he cannot get possession of the suit property. After that, defendant Nos. 2-4 in collusion with defendant No. 1 has been threatening the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the suit property on the basis of his forged and collusive deed dated 1-6-1983. Hence this suit has been filed.
